site.name: The Mouseion & Great Library
site.capacity: ancient estimates range wildly (tens of thousands to 400,000+ scrolls); no reliable figure survives

reconstruction_confidence.note: No remains of the Mouseion or Great Library have been securely identified. The site is known only approximately — the royal Brucheion quarter — and the architecture is entirely unattested. The model shown is a conjectural evocation, not a reconstruction from evidence.

site.evidence_summary: The most famous library of antiquity: part of the Mouseion ('shrine of the Muses'), a royal research institution founded by the first Ptolemies. Under librarians such as Zenodotus, Callimachus, Apollonius of Rhodes, Eratosthenes and Aristarchus it became the engine of Hellenistic scholarship — textual criticism, geography, mathematics, astronomy. Its size and its destruction are wrapped in ancient exaggeration and later legend; almost nothing of its physical form is known.
site.provenance_note: Of every library here, this is the one we know least as a building and most as a legend. The scholars below genuinely worked at Alexandria (Strong association); Callimachus's Pinakes was composed there, about the collection itself (Documented); the Iliad stands for the Alexandrian recension, the library's defining work of criticism (Comparative). None of it is an inventory of what physically sat on the shelves — no such inventory survives.
